subject: Emotions
title: Surprise in Education
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Surprise in Education.

hook.text: A physics teacher drops a bowling ball from a pendulum toward her face. She doesn't flinch. The class never forgets.

buildup.text: Surprise-based lessons activate the hippocampus more strongly. Students remember surprises weeks after the class.

discovery.text: The 'desirable difficulty' theory says mild confusion boosts learning. Surprise creates the right amount of struggle.

twist.text: But too much surprise overwhelms working memory. The best teachers calibrate novelty to the student's level.

climax.text: The Socratic method is a surprise engine: questions lead students to discover that their own assumptions were wrong.

punchline.text: The best teachers don't give answers. They break assumptions.

quiz.question: What does 'desirable difficulty' mean in learning?
